docs.title: scrapi
docs.text:
Turn any information set into a structured LLM analysis — in a single config file.

Point scrapi at your sources (web, documents, databases, financial data), describe what you want the LLM to extract and summarise, and get back a typed, auditable result — optionally rendered to a standalone report in your format of choice. No glue code. No prompt plumbing. Just configure and run.

import scrapi

config = scrapi.load_toml_config("config.toml")
result = scrapi.make_orchestrator(config).run()

print(result.summary.result)

docs.title: What can you build with it?
Financial research reports
docs.text: Combine live web search with market data to produce a structured company brief on demand. Each source is analysed individually, then all findings are aggregated into a single cross-source summary — complete with citations. The result can be rendered as a Markdown report and saved automatically.

docs.title: Customer feedback analysis
docs.text: Your customer survey responses sit in a database table. Point the SQL scraper at them, define what you want extracted (sentiment, topic, urgency), and let the LLM run structured inference over every row. Aggregate the individual results into an overall summary without writing a single line of prompt-management code.

docs.title: AI-assisted decision support
docs.text: Define a Pydantic schema that captures not just the decision outcome but also a mandatory explanation field. Feed the decision-relevant information set through scrapi, and each result is tagged with a structured rationale — traceable, auditable, and ready to feed into a downstream approval workflow.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
scrapi runs a three-stage pipeline:

flowchart LR
    cfg[TOML config] --> orch[Orchestrator]
    orch --> s1[Scraper 1]
    orch --> sN[Scraper N]
    s1 --> si1[Search Inference 1]
    sN --> siN[Search Inference N]
    si1 --> sum[Summary Inference]
    siN --> sum
    sum --> out[RunResult]
  1. Scrape — collect content from one or more sources (web, files, financial data, SQL)
  2. Search inference — run a structured LLM extraction on each individual result
  3. Summary inference — aggregate all results into a final cross-source summary
Concept Description Orchestrator Wires scrapers, inference, and renderer into a single run() call ScrapiConfig TOML-based configuration parsed into typed dataclasses BaseScraper Abstract interface all scrapers implement — yields BaseSearchResult objects Inference Single-shot structured LLM call; SearchInference and SummaryInference wrap it RunResult Iterable container holding ResultPair objects and the final summary

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: scrapi is configured with a TOML file. The required top-level sections are [llm], [inference], and [[scrapers]]. The [renderer] section is optional.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
[llm]
provider = "openai"

[llm.config]
azure_endpoint = "https://<your-resource>.openai.azure.com/"
model = "gpt-4.1"

[inference.search]
system_prompt = "You are a financial research analyst."
task_prompt = "Extract the key facts and sentiment from this source relevant to the company's situation and outlook."

[inference.summary]
system_prompt = "You are a financial research analyst."
task_prompt = "Based on all sources, summarise the company's current situation and outlook. Cite your sources."

[[scrapers]]
provider = "yahoo"
[scrapers.scrape]
query = "Apple latest company news"
n = 5

[[scrapers]]
provider = "finance"
[scrapers.scrape]
query = ["AAPL"]

[renderer]
provider = "markdown"
report_path = "~/report.md"

docs.title: [inference]
docs.text: Inference is split into two stages. Both are required.

docs.title: [inference.search]
docs.text:
Applied per-result to each individual search result.

Key Type Description system_prompt string System-level instruction for the LLM task_prompt string Per-result extraction instruction

docs.title: [inference.summary]
docs.text:
Applied once across all collected search inference results.

Key Type Description system_prompt string System-level instruction for the LLM task_prompt string Cross-source summary instruction

docs.title: [[scrapers]]
docs.text:
Each [[scrapers]] block defines one scraper. Multiple blocks can be combined in a single run.

Key Type Description provider string Scraper backend. One of yahoo, file, finance, sql, dummy.

docs.title: [scrapers.config] — provider-specific constructor args
docs.text: Some scrapers require a [scrapers.config] section (e.g. sql for the connection string).

docs.title: [scrapers.scrape] — arguments forwarded to scraper.scrape()
docs.text:
yahoofilefinancesqldummy Key Type Description query string Search query string n int Number of results to fetch Key Type Description query list[str] File paths or glob patterns. PDFs are converted via PyMuPDF4LLM; other formats via MarkItDown. Key Type Description query list[str] List of ticker symbols, e.g. ["AAPL", "MSFT"] Key Type Description query string SQL query to execute rows_as_results bool If true, each row becomes a separate SQLSearchResult; if false, the entire result set is one result rendered as a Markdown table

The sql scraper requires a [scrapers.config] section:

[[scrapers]]
provider = "sql"
[scrapers.config]
connection_string = "mssql+pymssql://user:${DB_PASSWORD}@host:1433/mydb"
[scrapers.scrape]
query = "SELECT * FROM schema.table"
rows_as_results = false

${VAR} placeholders in the connection string are resolved from environment variables at instantiation time and URL-encoded automatically.

Key Type Description query string Synthetic query label (used in result metadata) n int Number of synthetic results to generate

docs.title: Writing a Custom Scraper
docs.text: scrapi is designed to be extended. If the built-in scrapers don't cover your data source, you can write your own in a few lines and slot it straight into the pipeline.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
Every scraper must subclass BaseScraper and implement two methods:

Method What it does _scrape(*args, **kwargs) Fetches content and returns a list of BaseSearchResult objects. You define the parameter signature. convert_to_ai_content(raw_content) Converts raw content to a plain string suitable for LLM consumption.

The public scrape() method (inherited from BaseScraper) calls _scrape() and raises NoResultsFoundError if the result is empty or if an exception is raised — you do not need to implement it yourself.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from scrapi.scraping.base import BaseScraper
from scrapi.models.search_result import WebSearchResult, SuccessfulSearch, FailedSearch


class RSSFeedScraper(BaseScraper):
    """Fetches items from an RSS feed."""

    def __init__(self, feed_url: str) -> None:
        self.feed_url = feed_url

    def _scrape(self, n: int = 10) -> list[WebSearchResult]:
        import feedparser  # your own dependency

        feed = feedparser.parse(self.feed_url)
        results = []
        for entry in feed.entries[:n]:
            text = entry.get("summary", "")
            results.append(
                WebSearchResult(
                    scraper_repr=repr(self),
                    status=SuccessfulSearch(status=200),
                    fetched_at=datetime.now(),
                    source={"url": entry.get("link", "")},
                    raw_content=text,
                    ai_content=self.convert_to_ai_content(text),
                )
            )
        return results

    @staticmethod
    def convert_to_ai_content(raw_content: Any) -> str:
        return raw_content

docs.title: Choosing a result type
docs.text:
Pick the BaseSearchResult subtype that best describes your source. Using the right type helps renderers and downstream code interpret the result correctly.

Type When to use WebSearchResult Web pages, APIs, feeds — any URL-backed source FileSearchResult Local files on disk FinanceSearchResult Financial/market data (raw_content should be a FinancialSnapshot) SQLSearchResult Database rows (raw_content should be a list[dict]) BaseSearchResult Subclass directly if none of the above fit

docs.title: Handling errors
docs.text:
Set status to FailedSearch when a single item cannot be fetched, but still append the result so the pipeline sees all sources:

try:
    text = fetch_content(url)
    status = SuccessfulSearch(status=200)
except Exception as e:
    text = ""
    status = FailedSearch(status=0, message=str(e), error=e)

results.append(WebSearchResult(..., status=status, raw_content=text, ai_content=text))

This lets the inference stage skip failed results gracefully rather than aborting the whole run.

docs.title: Using your scraper programmatically
docs.text:
from scrapi import parse_config, make_orchestrator
from scrapi.scraping.base import BaseScraper  # or import your module

scraper = RSSFeedScraper(feed_url="https://feeds.example.com/news.rss")

# Use directly
results = scraper.scrape(n=5)

# Or wire into the orchestrator manually
from scrapi.orchestrator import Orchestrator
from scrapi.inference.search import SearchInference
from scrapi.inference.summary import SummaryInference

orchestrator = Orchestrator(
    scrapers=[(scraper, {"n": 5})],
    search_inference=search_inference,
    summary_inference=summary_inference,
)
result = orchestrator.run()

docs.title: Registering your scraper for TOML config
docs.text:
To use your scraper via make_orchestrator and a TOML config file, add it to SCRAPER_REGISTRY in scrapi/config/registry.py:

from my_package.scrapers import RSSFeedScraper

SCRAPER_REGISTRY = {
    ...,
    "rss": RSSFeedScraper,
}

Then reference it in your config like any built-in scraper:

[[scrapers]]
provider = "rss"

[scrapers.config]
feed_url = "https://feeds.example.com/news.rss"

[scrapers.scrape]
n = 10

Keys under [scrapers.config] are forwarded to __init__; keys under [scrapers.scrape] are forwarded to _scrape().

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.12+ and uv.

git clone git@github.com:dheimgartner/scrapi.git
cd scrapi
uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: 1. Write a config file
docs.text:
Create config.toml:

[llm]
provider = "openai"

[llm.config]
azure_endpoint = "https://<your-resource>.openai.azure.com/"
model = "gpt-4.1"

[inference.search]
system_prompt = "You are a financial research analyst."
task_prompt = "Extract the key facts and sentiment from this source relevant to the company's situation."

[inference.summary]

task_prompt = "Summarise the company's current situation and outlook. Cite your sources."

[[scrapers]]

query = "Apple latest company news"

[renderer]

docs.title: 2. Set environment variables
docs.text:
export AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY="..."
# or for Anthropic:
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="..."

docs.title: 3. Run
docs.text:
import scrapi

config = scrapi.load_toml_config("config.toml")
orchestrator = scrapi.make_orchestrator(config)
result = orchestrator.run()

print(result.summary.result)

The rendered Markdown report is saved to ~/report.md.

docs.title: Iterating over results
docs.text:
for pair in result:
    print(pair.search.source)       # source URL / path / ticker
    print(pair.inference.result)    # per-source LLM verdict

docs.title: Programmatic config
docs.text:
No TOML file required — build the config dict directly:

from scrapi import parse_config, make_orchestrator

config = parse_config({
    "llm": {
        "provider": "anthropic",
        "config": {"model": "claude-opus-4-7"},
    },
    "inference": {
        "search": {
            "system_prompt": "You are a research analyst.",
            "task_prompt": "Extract the key facts from this source.",
        },
        "summary": {
            "system_prompt": "You are a research analyst.",
            "task_prompt": "Summarise all sources. Cite them.",
        },
    },
    "scrapers": [
        {"provider": "yahoo", "scrape": {"query": "Apple Q1 2025 earnings", "n": 3}},
    ],
})

orchestrator = make_orchestrator(config)
result = orchestrator.run()

docs.title: Standalone Inference
docs.text:
Use Inference directly without the orchestrator:

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from scrapi.scraping.dummy import DummyScraper
from scrapi.inference import Inference

class RiskSchema(BaseModel):
    summary: str = Field(description="One-sentence summary.")
    risk: str = Field(description="Key risk identified in the source.")

scraper = DummyScraper()
results = scraper.scrape(query="Apple earnings", n=3)

inference = Inference(
    llm=llm,
    system_prompt="You are a risk analyst.",
    task_prompt="Identify the main risk.",
    schema=RiskSchema,
)

for result in results:
    ir = inference.run(result)
    print(ir.structured_output.risk)

docs.title: Manual rendering
docs.text:
from scrapi.renderer.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

renderer = MarkdownRenderer(report_path="report.md")
renderer.render(result)
renderer.save()

render() returns the document as a string and caches it internally. save() writes the cache to report_path.

docs.title: Inference
docs.text:
scrapi provides three inference classes:

  • Inference — generic single-shot structured LLM call; bring your own Pydantic schema
  • SearchInference — wraps Inference with the built-in SearchSchema
  • SummaryInference — wraps Inference with the built-in SummarySchema

The Orchestrator uses SearchInference and SummaryInference internally, but Inference can be used standalone against any scraper output.

docs.text:
Fetches search results, analyses each, and aggregates to a final summary.

Iterates over all scrapers, fetches results via each scraper's fetch kwargs, runs per-result inference on each, then runs summary-level inference over all collected results.

docs.title: Scrapers
docs.text: All scrapers inherit from BaseScraper and implement a _scrape() method that returns a list of BaseSearchResult objects. The public scrape() method wraps _scrape() and raises NoResultsFoundError on empty or failed results.

docs.title: BaseScraper
docs.text:
Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for content scrapers.

All scraper implementations must provide a mechanism for retrieving content from a data source and converting it into a collection of BaseSearchResult objects.

Implementations may obtain their content from search engines, web pages, APIs, document repositories, or other external systems, but should expose a consistent interface through scrape().

docs.title: _scrape(*args, **kwargs) abstractmethod
docs.text:
Retrieve content.

Implementations are responsible for executing the query against their respective data source, collecting the results, and returning them as search results. Each subclass defines its own parameter signature.

Returns:

Type Description list[BaseSearchResult]

list[BaseSearchResult]: Retrieved content represented as base search result.

docs.title: scrape(*args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Retrieve content, raising NoResultsFoundError on failure.

Wraps _scrape and raises if the result is empty or if the underlying implementation raises any exception.
